assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuine invention with a clear original experiment: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice proposal and its realization turned atomic clocks into a platform with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. It opens a door to measurements that could not be made before (relativistic geodesy, tests of constancy of constants, a candidate for redefining the second). Strong fit to the discovery-or-invention criterion.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Jun Ye's group made the decisive demonstrations of record accuracy and stability with Sr. Two names give a clean, fair configuration. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow/Oates) contributed but are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups worldwide with sub-1e-18 comparisons; the technology is mature and recognition is timely. Atomic-clock physics was last recognized in 1989 and 2012, so this is a distinct advance.
uncertainties: Whether the proposal or the first operational clock best defines the original contribution, and the role of other early groups, should be checked against the historical record.
Not certain of every detail of the early priority sequence from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene produced correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable, clean, controllable platform, and founded the field of twistronics. The experiments are original and an unmistakable opening of a new class of materials that can be seen and tuned with scanning probes and transport.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at the magic angle (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations with the Cao et al. papers. This theory-plus-experiment pairing is a fair three-person configuration, although the experimental credit also extends to the co-first author Yuan Cao, who is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups across several material platforms within a few years, which is quick and robust. Interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still debated, but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Exclusion of Yuan Cao and the question of whether the experimental credit is wholly captured are open attribution issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance observed in 1995 was the original experiment that made magnetic tunnel junctions viable, with huge technological consequences in read heads and MRAM. It is a measured, reproducible effect with wide societal benefit.
assessment.attribution: Moodera (MIT) and Miyazaki (Tohoku) independently reported the room-temperature effect in 1995. Parkin is the third credited name on the list, but his contribution is mostly the later MgO and giant-effect optimization, so I leave him out in favor of the original discovery. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature observation is background and the priority question is a real one.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and commercially deployed for more than two decades, so it is fully mature. The prize for GMR in 2007 was close in subject, which makes this a potentially redundant topic.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2007 GMR prize may make it appear a lesser step.
Priority relative to Julliere (1975) and the role of Parkin versus the MgO breakthroughs (Parkin and Yuasa) need to be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and quantized edge transport are among the most important developments in condensed-matter physics of the last two decades. The experimental realizations (HgTe quantum wells, and zero-field quantized conductance in magnetically doped films) are original verifications of predicted phases, and they are essentially measured transport quantities that anyone can check.
assessment.attribution: Kane provided the decisive theory of the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group made the original experimental observation in HgTe; Xue's group first realized the quantum anomalous Hall effect experimentally. A three-way split covers both the theory and two experiments but omits Mele, Hasan, Zhang, Bernevig and Dai/Fang, and so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by independent groups, and the QAH is now a metrology tool. The very large number of contributors makes a compact prize difficult and could argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Many candidate contributors (Mele, Zhang, Hasan, Dai, Fang, Hughes) and a compound discovery whose parts could need different recognition.
The distinct entries on this longlist for the same field overlap, so the exact configuration is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins turned a defect in diamond into a room-temperature quantum sensor and qubit. This is a new tool that opens a door to nanoscale magnetic, electric and temperature sensing, including in biology and materials, close to my own interest in what can be imaged atom by atom.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Gruber (1997) showed optical detection of single NV centers; Jelezko and Wrachtrup demonstrated coherent control. Lukin's group contributed major NV sensing and quantum-register work, but this is later and broader. Credit allocation is plausible but the original single-spin ODMR demonstration involved other authors, such as Gruber, who are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups and in widespread use, with applications progressing quickly. The field is still evolving, so some of the technological payoffs are not yet fully realized.
uncertainties: Whether Lukin's role is original discovery or later extension.
Other early contributors, including Gruber, Drabenstedt and Hanson, are not covered by the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire gain media and passive mode-locking, including Kerr-lens and semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors, created the modern femtosecond laser. It underlies attosecond science, which was recognized in 2023, and also spectroscopy, microscopy and frequency combs. It is an invention of great reach.
assessment.attribution: Moulton demonstrated the Ti:sapphire laser; Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking (1991); Keller invented the SESAM. The three roles are distinct and each is original, but the question of whether the invention is a single discovery is an issue. Keller's inclusion would also add a woman laureate, which I welcome only as a secondary consideration, not as a criterion.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universal, and long confirmed. The risk is that it looks like an enabling technology already partly recognized through chirped-pulse amplification (2018) and attosecond physics (2023).
uncertainties: Competing credit among Spence, Kean and Sibbett versus Keller, and the share of Moulton's contribution, are not fully clear to me from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells went from a few percent to over 25 percent efficiency within a decade, with benefit to energy supply. The materials science is interesting and the experimental progress is original.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park and Gratzel produced the solid-state cell (2012), and Snaith's group showed the meso-superstructured cell and thin-film route. Gratzel and Kanatzidis are not on this list and the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view: long-term stability, lead toxicity and manufacturing at scale are still unproven, and the discovery is as much engineering as physics. Better recognized later if commercialization is established.
uncertainties: Whether this is a physics prize topic and whether the credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith and Gratzel is fair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux, and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources, opened neutrino astronomy as a new window. The measurement is original and was experimentally verified in a remarkable instrument.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the key proponent and leader of IceCube, Karle a central figure in its development and Yoshida a major contributor. A collaboration of hundreds of members makes an individual attribution difficult, and the original AMANDA and Baikal work complicates the history.
assessment.maturity: Increasingly strong, though source identification is based on a few associations at moderate significance and the origin of most of the flux is unknown. Timing is plausible but a little early.
uncertainties: Large collaboration and ambiguous individual credit.
Only a few source associations at modest significance.
